proofs.proof_tex:
Put \(t=m/n\).  The aspect-ratio assumption gives \(t\in[c_-,c_+]\).  Choose \(c_0<1\).  On \(b_{nm}\le c_0\), the truncation in \(\mathrm{def:frontier\mbox{-}rate}\) is inactive, and hence
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 b_{nm}
 &=\frac{B}{\lambda_{nm}}K r^{3/2}\mu q^{-1/2}
   \sqrt{\log(en)}\sqrt{nm}\sqrt{n^{-1}+nm^{-2}}\\
 &=K r^{3/2}\mu\sqrt{t+t^{-1}}
   \frac{B}{\lambda_{nm}}\sqrt{\frac{n\log(en)}q}.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{1}
\]
Thus, with
\[
 s_{nm}:=\frac{B}{\lambda_{nm}}
 \sqrt{\frac{n\log(en)}q},
\]
there are constants \(C_-,C_+>0\), depending only on \(r,K,\mu,c_-,c_+\), such that
\[
 C_-s_{nm}\le b_{nm}\le C_+s_{nm}.
 \tag{2}
\]

We construct a constant-propensity subexperiment.  Because \(r\) is fixed, partition \(I\) into balanced disjoint blocks \(I_1,\ldots,I_r\) and \(J\) into balanced disjoint blocks \(J_1,\ldots,J_r\).  Write \(N_s=|I_s|\) and \(M_s=|J_s|\).  For \(s\ge2\), let \(u_s=N_s^{-1/2}{\bf1}_{I_s}\), and for every \(s\), let \(v_s=M_s^{-1/2}{\bf1}_{J_s}\).  Let \(u_0=N_1^{-1/2}{\bf1}_{I_1}\), fix \(k_0\in I_1\), and, for \(k\in\mathcal K:=I_1\setminus\{k_0\}\), set
\[
 w_k=\frac{e_k-e_{k_0}}{\sqrt2},\qquad
 \delta=a\frac{B}{\lambda_{nm}}
 \sqrt{\frac{\log(en)}q},\qquad
 u_k=\frac{u_0+\delta w_k}{\sqrt{1+\delta^2}}.
 \tag{3}
\]
Here \(a>0\) is fixed below.  The vectors \(u_0,w_k\) are orthogonal unit vectors.  Disjoint block supports therefore show that
\[
 U_k=(u_k,u_2,\ldots,u_r)\in\mathbb O_{n,r},
 \qquad V=(v_1,\ldots,v_r)\in\mathbb O_{m,r}.
\]
Also put \(U_0=(u_0,u_2,\ldots,u_r)\) and
\[
 M_k=\lambda_{nm}U_kV^\top,
 \qquad M_0=\lambda_{nm}U_0V^\top.
 \tag{4}
\]

We verify the class restrictions.  Equations (2)--(3) give
\[
 \delta\sqrt n=a s_{nm}\le aC_-^{-1}b_{nm}le aC_-^{-1}c_0.
 \tag{5}
\]
For rows in \(I_1\),
\[
 \lVert e_i^\top U_k\rVert_2
 \le N_1^{-1/2}+\delta/\sqrt2,
 \tag{6}
\]
and for rows in \(I_s\), \(s\ge2\), the row norm is \(N_s^{-1/2}\).  Balanced blocks and fixed \(r\) give \(\max_s\sqrt{n/N_s}\to\sqrt r\).  Since \(\mu>1\), there is strict slack below \(\sqrt{\mu r}\).  Choose \(ac_0\) small enough using (5), and then take \(n\) large enough; (5)--(6) yield
\[
 \lVert U_k\rVert_{2,\infty}\le\sqrt{\mu r/n}.
 \tag{7}
\]
The same balanced-block calculation without a perturbation gives
\[
 \lVert V\rVert_{2,\infty}\le\sqrt{\mu r/m}
 \tag{8}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(m\).  Equations (7)--(8) verify both incoherence assumptions.  By (4), all \(r\) nonzero singular values of \(M_k\) equal \(\lambda_{nm}\); hence exact rank, the signal floor, and the condition-number bound hold, the last because \(K\ge1\).

For large dimensions, balanced blocks satisfy \(N_s\ge n/(2r)\) and \(M_s\ge m/(2r)\).  Equations (3)--(4) imply
\[
 \max_{i,j}|(M_k)_{ij}|
 \le \frac{2r\lambda_{nm}}{\sqrt{nm}}
 +aB\sqrt{\frac{2r\log(en)}{qm}}.
 \tag{9}
\]
Choose \(c_1>0\) such that \(2rc_1\le1/4\).  Under \(\lambda_{nm}\le c_1B\sqrt{nm}\), the first term in (9) is at most \(B/4\); the second is at most \(B/4\) eventually by bounded aspect ratio and fixed \(q,r,a\).  Thus
\[
 \max_{i,j}|(M_k)_{ij}|\le B/2.
 \tag{10}
\]

For \(k\in\mathcal K\cup\{0\}\), define \(P_k\) as follows.  Set \(Y_{ij}(0)=0\).  Independently over cells draw \(Y_{ij}(1)\in\{-B,B\}\) with
\[
 P_k\{Y_{ij}(1)=B\}
 =h_{k,ij}:=\frac12\left(1+\frac{(M_k)_{ij}}B\right).
 \tag{11}
\]
Independently of all potential outcomes and independently over cells, draw \(A_{ij}\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(q)\), and record \(p_{ij}=q\).  Equation (10) puts \(h_{k,ij}\in[1/4,3/4]\), while (11) gives \(E_{P_k}[Y_{ij}(1)]=(M_k)_{ij}\).  Independence from the row-major past gives
\[
 \mu^1_{ij}=(M_k)_{ij},\qquad \mu^0_{ij}=0,
 \qquad M=\mu^1-\mu^0=M_k.
 \tag{12}
\]
Thus the causal effect is obtained from the potential-outcome conditional means, not stipulated through the observed score.  Independence of the current assignment from the potential outcomes conditional on the past verifies sequential randomization.  The equality \(p_{ij}=q\), with \(q<1/2\), verifies overlap, and the support in (11) verifies bounded outcomes.  Equations (7)--(8), the singular-value calculation, and the assumed aspect condition verify all remaining member properties.  Consequently
\[
 P_k\in\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{pred}}_{n,m}(r,\mu,K,q,B,\lambda)
 \quad(k\in\mathcal K\cup\{0\}).
 \tag{13}
\]

We bound the information in \(\mathcal O_{n,m}=\sigma(A,Y,p)\).  If \(x,y\in[-B/2,B/2]\), put \(s=(1+x/B)/2\) and \(t'=(1+y/B)/2\).  The Bernoulli relative entropy \(f(s)=s\log(s/t')+(1-s)\log((1-s)/(1-t'))\) satisfies \(f(t')=f'(t')=0\) and
\[
 f''(s)=\frac1{s(1-s)}\le\frac{16}3
 \quad\text{on }[1/4,3/4].
\]
Taylor's theorem gives
\[
 \operatorname{kl}\left(\frac{1+x/B}{2},
 \frac{1+y/B}{2}\right)
 \le\frac{2}{3}\frac{(x-y)^2}{B^2}.
 \tag{14}
\]
The assignment law and recorded propensity coincide under \(P_k\) and \(P_0\).  Given \(A_{ij}=0\), the observed outcome is the common zero; given \(A_{ij}=1\), it has Bernoulli sign parameter \(h_{k,ij}\).  Independence over cells, (14), and direct factorization of the product likelihood yield
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(P_k^{\mathcal O},P_0^{\mathcal O})
 \le \frac{Cq}{B^2}\lVert M_k-M_0\rVert_F^2.
 \tag{15}
\]
Only the first singular component differs, so
\[
 \lVert M_k-M_0\rVert_F^2
 =\lambda_{nm}^2\lVert u_k-u_0\rVert_2^2.
\]
Orthogonality in (3) gives
\[
 \lVert u_k-u_0\rVert_2^2
 =2\left(1-\frac1{\sqrt{1+\delta^2}}\right)
 \le\delta^2.
\]
Substitution into (15) proves
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(P_k^{\mathcal O},P_0^{\mathcal O})
 \le Ca^2\log(en).
 \tag{16}
\]

The alternatives are separated in rowwise loss.  If \(k,l\in\mathcal K\) are distinct, inspect row \(k\).  Right multiplication by an orthogonal matrix preserves its Euclidean norm, and (3) gives
\[
 \lVert e_k^\top U_k\rVert_2-
 \lVert e_k^\top U_l\rVert_2
 =\frac{\delta}{\sqrt{2(1+\delta^2)}}.
\]
The reverse triangle inequality therefore gives
\[
 \mathcal L(U_k,U_l)
 \ge\Delta_{nm}:=sqrt{\frac n{\mu r}}
 \frac{\delta}{\sqrt{2(1+\delta^2)}}.
 \tag{17}
\]
Equation (5) makes \(\delta\le1\) eventually.  From (1), (3), and bounded aspect ratio,
\[
 \frac{\sqrt{n/(\mu r)}\,\delta}{b_{nm}}
 =\frac{a}{K r^2\mu^{3/2}\sqrt{t+t^{-1}}},
\]
so there is a constant \(c>0\) depending only on the fixed quantities such that
\[
 \Delta_{nm}\ge c b_{nm}.
 \tag{18}
\]

We finally derive the testing reduction.  Let \(D=|\mathcal K|=N_1-1\), let \(\Theta\) be uniform on \(\mathcal K\), and conditionally on \(\Theta=k\) draw the observation from \(P_k^{\mathcal O}\).  With \(\overline P=D^{-1}\sum_kP_k^{\mathcal O}\), direct expansion of log likelihood ratios gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 I(\Theta;\mathcal O)
 &=\frac1D\sum_k\operatorname{KL}(P_k^{\mathcal O},\overline P)\\
 &=\frac1D\sum_k\operatorname{KL}(P_k^{\mathcal O},P_0^{\mathcal O})
   -\operatorname{KL}(\overline P,P_0^{\mathcal O})\\
 &\le Ca^2\log(en),
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{19}
\]
where the inequality uses nonnegativity of relative entropy and (16).  For any decoder \(\widehat\Theta\), put \(P_e=P(\widehat\Theta\ne\Theta)\).  Conditioning the entropy of \(\Theta\) on the error indicator gives
\[
 H(\Theta\mid\mathcal O)\le\log2+P_e\log D.
\]
Since \(H(\Theta)=\log D\), (19) yields
\[
 P_e\ge1-\frac{Ca^2\log(en)+\log2}{\log D}.
 \tag{20}
\]
Balanced blocks give \(D\asymp n\).  Choose \(a>0\) sufficiently small so that the right side of (20) is at least \(1/2\) eventually.

For any \(\widetilde U\in\mathfrak E_{n,m}\), decode by a nearest member of \(\{U_k:k\in\mathcal K\}\) in orthogonal-quotient \(2,\infty\) distance.  That distance obeys the triangle inequality: compose optimizing orthogonal alignments and use invariance of row norms under right orthogonal multiplication.  Thus a decoding error under \(P_k\), together with (17), implies
\[
 \mathcal L(\widetilde U,U_k)\ge\Delta_{nm}/2.
\]
Averaging over the uniform index, applying (20), and then (18), gives
\[
 \sup_{k\in\mathcal K}E_{P_k}[\mathcal L(\widetilde U,U_k)]
 \ge\frac{\Delta_{nm}}4
 \ge c_2b_{nm}.
\]
By (13), this finite family is a constant-propensity subset of the frozen predictable class.  Taking the supremum over that class and then the infimum over \(\widetilde U\in\mathfrak E_{n,m}\) proves the theorem.

Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:ipw\mbox{-}expected\mbox{-}risk\mbox{-}upper}\) gives the stronger uniform first-moment statement
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{pred}}_{n,m}}
 E_P\!\left[\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm I},U)\right]
 \le C a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}.
\]
The radius is strictly positive because \(B>0\), \(q>0\), \(\lambda_{nm}>0\), and \(n,m\ge2\).  Therefore Markov's inequality gives, for every \(t>0\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{pred}}_{n,m}}
 P\!\left\{\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm I},U)>
 t a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\right\}\le \frac Ct.
\]
This is the asserted uniform \(O_P(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm})\) bound.  The radius and the moment proof use only the score matrix and contain no loading family, so no factor depending on \(|\mathcal G_n|\) occurs.

For the final assertion, Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:adaptive\mbox{-}endogenous\mbox{-}target\mbox{-}obstruction}\) supplies a sequence \(P_n\) in the same class and constants \(c_0,c_1>0\) such that \(b_{nn}\to0\) and
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}P_n\!\left\{
 \mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm I},U)>c_0\right\}\ge c_1.
\]
If the IPW--SVD loss were uniformly \(O_P(b_{nm})\), then for \(\varepsilon=c_1/2\) some fixed \(T<\infty\) would make the displayed probability at threshold \(Tb_{nn}\) at most \(\varepsilon\) eventually.  Since \(Tb_{nn}<c_0\) eventually, this contradicts the preceding lower probability.  The witness evaluates \(\widehat U^{\mathrm I}\) and hence proves no impossibility statement for a different estimator.

Fix \(P\) in the predictable class and expose cells in the row-major order of \(\mathrm{def:global\mbox{-}filtration}\).  By Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:ipw\mbox{-}identification}\), each \(E_{ij}\) has conditional mean zero given \(\mathbb G_{o(i,j)-1}\).  Sequential randomization, bounded outcomes, and overlap give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 E_P\!\left[(Z^{\mathrm{ipw}}_{ij})^2
 \mid\mathbb G_{o(i,j)-1}\right]
 &=E_P\!\left[
 \frac{Y_{ij}(1)^2}{p_{ij}}+
 \frac{Y_{ij}(0)^2}{1-p_{ij}}
 \mathrel{\Big|}\mathbb G_{o(i,j)-1}\right]\\
 &\le \frac{2B^2}{q}.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{1}
\]
For the equality, condition first on both potential outcomes and use \(P(A_{ij}=1\mid\mathbb G_{o(i,j)-1},Y_{ij}(0),Y_{ij}(1))=p_{ij}\); both divisions are valid because \(q\le p_{ij}\le1-q\).  Since \(M_{ij}=E_P[Z^{\mathrm{ipw}}_{ij}\mid\mathbb G_{o(i,j)-1}]\), conditional variance is no larger than (1).  Moreover \(|Z^{\mathrm{ipw}}_{ij}|\le B/q\), \(|M_{ij}|\le2B\), and \(q<1/2\), whence
\[
 |E_{ij}|\le \frac{2B}{q}.
 \tag{2}
\]

Introduce the self-adjoint dilation
\[
 \Delta_{ij}=
 \begin{pmatrix}
 0&E_{ij}e_ie_j^\top\\
 E_{ij}e_je_i^\top&0
 \end{pmatrix}.
\]
Its norm is \(|E_{ij}|\), and its square has diagonal blocks \(E_{ij}^2e_ie_i^\top\) and \(E_{ij}^2e_je_j^\top\).  Therefore (1) implies
\[
 \left\lVert\sum_{i,j}E_P[\Delta_{ij}^2
 \mid\mathbb G_{o(i,j)-1}]\right\rVert
 \le v_{nm}:=\frac{2B^2(n\vee m)}q.
 \tag{3}
\]
Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:tropp\mbox{-}matrix\mbox{-}freedman}\), applied to both signs of this \((n+m)\)-dimensional martingale using (2)--(3), gives
\[
 P\{\lVert E\rVert\ge t\}
 \le2(n+m)\exp\!\left\{-\frac{t^2/2}{v_{nm}+R_{nm}t/3}\right\},
 \qquad R_{nm}=\frac{2B}{q}.
 \tag{4}
\]
The terminal dilation has operator norm \(\lVert E\rVert\).  Put \(L_{nm}=\log(2(n+m))\).  Solving the quadratic inequality in (4) shows that, for every \(x\ge0\),
\[
 P\!\left\{\lVert E\rVert>
 \sqrt{2v_{nm}(L_{nm}+x)}+
 \frac{2R_{nm}}3(L_{nm}+x)\right\}\le e^{-x}.
 \tag{5}
\]
Integrating (5), using \(\sqrt{L_{nm}+x}\le\sqrt{L_{nm}}+\sqrt x\), \(\int_0^\infty e^{-x}\,dx=1\), and \(\int_0^\infty e^{-x}\sqrt x\,dx<\infty\), yields
\[
 E_P\lVert E\rVert
 \le C B\left\{
 \sqrt{\frac{(n\vee m)\log(e(n+m))}{q}}+
 \frac{\log(e(n+m))}{q}\right\}
 =:C\eta_{nm}.
 \tag{6}
\]
Every bound is uniform in \(P\).

It remains to pass from operator error to the declared loss without assuming predictability of the singular factors.  Let \(P_U=UU^\top\), and let \((\widehat U,\widehat\Sigma,\widehat V)\) be the leading rank-\(r\) singular triple of \(M+E\).  Exact rank gives \((I-P_U)M=0\).  The signal floor and the singular-value min--max formula imply, on \(\{\lVert E\rVert\le\lambda_{nm}/2\}\),
\[
 \sigma_r(\widehat\Sigma)
 \ge\sigma_r(M)-\lVert E\rVert
 \ge\lambda_{nm}-\lVert E\rVert>0.
\]
Projecting \((M+E)\widehat V=\widehat U\widehat\Sigma\) onto the orthogonal complement of \(U\) therefore gives
\[
 \lVert(I-P_U)\widehat U\rVert
 \le\frac{\lVert E\rVert}{\lambda_{nm}-\lVert E\rVert}
 \le\frac{2\lVert E\rVert}{\lambda_{nm}}.
 \tag{7}
\]
Diagonalizing the principal-angle cosines of \(U^\top\widehat U\) and using \(2(1-\cos t)\le2\sin^2t\) supplies \(R\in\mathbb O_r\) such that
\[
 \lVert\widehat UR-U\rVert
 \le\sqrt2\lVert(I-P_U)\widehat U\rVert.
 \tag{8}
\]
Off the event in (7), the left side of (8) is at most two.  Since \(\lVert Q\rVert_{2,\infty}\le\lVert Q\rVert\), the two cases combine to give
\[
 \mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm I},U)
 \le C\sqrt{\frac n{\mu r}}
 \left(1\wedge\frac{\lVert E\rVert}{\lambda_{nm}}\right).
 \tag{9}
\]
The fixed tie rule ensures that the leading left singular vectors of \(\mathcal P_r(M+E)\) are the selected leading left singular vectors of \(M+E\).  Finally, concavity of \(x\mapsto1\wedge x\), Jensen's inequality, and (6) yield
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 E_P\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm I},U)
 &\le C\sqrt{\frac n{\mu r}}
 E_P\left[1\wedge\frac{\lVert E\rVert}{\lambda_{nm}}\right]\\
 &\le C\sqrt{\frac n{\mu r}}
 \left(1\wedge\frac{\eta_{nm}}{\lambda_{nm}}\right)
 =C a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Taking the supremum over the declared class proves the proposition.

added_lemmas.statement:
The discrete-sine matrix \(U^{\mathrm F}\) belongs to \(\mathbb O_{n,r}\) and satisfies
\[
 \lVert U^{\mathrm F}\rVert_{2,\infty}
 \le\sqrt{\frac{2r}{n+1}}.
\]
Consequently, for every target \(U\) satisfying \(\lVert U\rVert_{2,\infty}\le\sqrt{\mu r/n}\), the pathwise bound
\[
 \mathcal L(U^{\mathrm F},U)
 \le1+\sqrt{\frac2\mu}
\]
holds.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Put \(x=\pi/(n+1)\).  For integers \(t\) with \(1\le t\le2n\), the geometric-series identity, followed by taking real parts, gives
\[
 C_t:=\sum_{i=1}^n\cos(itx)
 =\frac{\sin(ntx/2)\cos((n+1)tx/2)}{\sin(tx/2)}.
 \tag{1}
\]
The denominator is nonzero because \(0<tx/2<\pi\).  If \(t\) is odd, the cosine in the numerator is \(\cos(t\pi/2)=0\), so \(C_t=0\).  If \(t=2s\) is even, then \(1\le s\le n\), and
\[
 \sin\!\left(\frac{ns\pi}{n+1}\right)
 =\sin\!\left(s\pi-\frac{s\pi}{n+1}\right)
 =(-1)^{s+1}\sin\!\left(\frac{s\pi}{n+1}\right),
\]
while \(\cos(s\pi)=(-1)^s\).  Equation (1) therefore yields \(C_t=-1\).  Also set \(C_0=n\).

For \(1\le k,l\le n\), the product-to-sum identity now gives
\[
 \sum_{i=1}^n\sin(ikx)\sin(ilx)
 =\frac12\{C_{|k-l|}-C_{k+l}\}.
 \tag{2}
\]
When \(k\ne l\), the two indices \(|k-l|\) and \(k+l\) have the same parity and lie between one and \(2n\); the preceding evaluation of \(C_t\) makes the right side of (2) zero.  When \(k=l\), it equals \((C_0-C_{2k})/2=(n+1)/2\).  Multiplication by \(2/(n+1)\) proves that all \(n\) columns of the discrete-sine matrix are orthonormal.  Since \(r\le n\), its first \(r\) columns therefore satisfy
\[
 (U^{\mathrm F})^\top U^{\mathrm F}=I_r,
 \]
which is precisely \(U^{\mathrm F}\in\mathbb O_{n,r}\).

For every row \(i\), \(|\sin(\pi ik/(n+1))|\le1\), so the construction gives
\[
 \lVert e_i^\top U^{\mathrm F}\rVert_2^2
 =\frac2{n+1}\sum_{k=1}^r
 \sin^2\!\left(\frac{\pi ik}{n+1}\right)
 \le\frac{2r}{n+1}.
 \tag{3}
\]
Taking the maximum over \(i\) proves the first bound.  For the target, \(\mathrm{ass:left\mbox{-}incoherence}\) gives
\(\lVert U\rVert_{2,\infty}\le\sqrt{\mu r/n}\).  Choosing the admissible alignment \(R=I_r\) in \(\mathrm{def:rowwise\mbox{-}loss}\), applying the rowwise triangle inequality, and then using (3), we obtain
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathcal L(U^{\mathrm F},U)
 &\le\sqrt{\frac n{\mu r}}
 \left(\lVert U^{\mathrm F}\rVert_{2,\infty}
       +\lVert U\rVert_{2,\infty}\right)\\
 &\le\sqrt{\frac n{\mu r}}
 \left(\sqrt{\frac{2r}{n+1}}+sqrt{\frac{\mu r}{n}}\right)\\
 &=1+\sqrt{\frac{2n}{\mu(n+1)}}
 \le1+\sqrt{\frac2\mu}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
All inequalities are deterministic, so the conclusion holds pathwise.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every \(n,m\ge2\), the hybrid estimator \(\widehat U^{\mathrm H}\) is a member of \(\mathfrak E_{n,m}\).  There is a universal constant \(C<\infty\) such that
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{pred}}_{n,m}(r,\mu,K,q,B,\lambda)}
 E_P\!\left[\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm H},U)\right]
 \le C\{1\wedge a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\}.
\]
The estimator is the single data-driven map in \(\mathrm{def:hybrid\mbox{-}estimator}\); it is not a law-dependent oracle choice.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The recorded score is a measurable function of \((A,Y,p)\), and the rank projection with its fixed tie rule is measurable.  Thus \(\widehat U^{\mathrm I}\) is \(\mathcal O_{n,m}\)-measurable.  The fallback \(U^{\mathrm F}\) and the predicate \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\le1\) are deterministic functions of the fixed dimensions and envelopes.  The two-branch definition therefore makes \(\widehat U^{\mathrm H}\) \(\mathcal O_{n,m}\)-measurable.  Both branches lie in \(\mathbb O_{n,r}\), by the definition of \(\widehat U^{\mathrm I}\) and Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:discrete\mbox{-}sine\mbox{-}fallback\mbox{-}bound}\).  The definition of \(\mathfrak E_{n,m}\) consequently gives
\[
 \widehat U^{\mathrm H}\in\mathfrak E_{n,m}.
 \tag{1}
\]

The radius \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\) is deterministic and positive because \(n,m\ge2\), \(B>0\), \(q>0\), \(\lambda_{nm}>0\), \(r\ge1\), and \(\mu\ge1\).  If \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\le1\), the hybrid equals \(\widehat U^{\mathrm I}\), and Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:ipw\mbox{-}expected\mbox{-}risk\mbox{-}upper}\) gives
\[
 \sup_P E_P[\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm H},U)]
 \le C_1a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}
 =C_1\{1\wedge a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\}.
 \tag{2}
\]
If \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}>1\), the hybrid equals \(U^{\mathrm F}\).  Every law in the predictable class satisfies left incoherence, so the pathwise fallback lemma and \(\mu\ge1\) yield
\[
 \mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm H},U)
 \le1+\sqrt{2/\mu}
 \le1+\sqrt2
 =(1+\sqrt2)\{1\wedge a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\}.
 \tag{3}
\]
Taking expectations and the supremum over the same class preserves (3).  Equations (2)--(3), with \(C=\max\{C_1,1+\sqrt2\}\), prove the asserted uniform risk bound.  Since the branch is selected only by a deterministic radius, (1) also proves that the witness is one admissible data map rather than a per-law family.

added_lemmas.statement:
Fix \(r\), \(K\), and \(\mu>1\).  There are constants \(c_0,c_1,c,C>0\), depending only on these fixed quantities, \(q\), and the aspect bounds, such that, for all sufficiently large \(n,m\), whenever \(b_{nm}\le c_0\) and \(\lambda_{nm}\le c_1B\sqrt{nm}\),
\[
 c b_{nm}\le
 \inf_{\widetilde U\in\mathfrak E_{n,m}}
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{pred}}_{n,m}(r,\mu,K,q,B,\lambda)}
 E_P[\mathcal L(\widetilde U,U)]
 \le
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{pred}}_{n,m}(r,\mu,K,q,B,\lambda)}
 E_P[\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm H},U)]
 \le C\{1\wedge a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\}.
\]
In particular the minimax upper endpoint is at most a constant.  Separately, recorded IPW--SVD retains its \(C a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\) expected-risk guarantee and its estimator-specific \(b_{nm}\)-scale obstruction.  The latter does not prove that every estimator has constant-order risk, so the displayed \(b_{nm}\)-to-constant bracket need not be tight.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The first inequality is Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:adaptive\mbox{-}minimax\mbox{-}lower}\), under exactly its stated restrictions on \(b_{nm}\), \(\lambda_{nm}\), fixed complexity, overlap, and aspect ratio.  Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:hybrid\mbox{-}expected\mbox{-}risk\mbox{-}upper}\) proves that \(\widehat U^{\mathrm H}\in\mathfrak E_{n,m}\).  Evaluating the infimum over \(\mathfrak E_{n,m}\) at this one admissible estimator proves the middle inequality, and the expected-risk conclusion of that same proposition proves the last inequality.  Since \(1\wedge a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\le1\), its last member is at most \(C\).

Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:ipw\mbox{-}expected\mbox{-}risk\mbox{-}upper}\) separately gives
\[
 \sup_P E_P[\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm I},U)]
 \le C'a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}.
\]
Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:adaptive\mbox{-}endogenous\mbox{-}target\mbox{-}obstruction}\) concerns only \(\widehat U^{\mathrm I}\).  It therefore cannot increase the minimax lower endpoint, whose infimum ranges over all of \(\mathfrak E_{n,m}\).  This proves both the bracket and the stated limitation.

proposed.name: Loose recorded-IPW spectral radius
proposed.construction:
Define
\[
 a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}=
 \sqrt{\frac n{\mu r}}\left[1\wedge
 \frac B{\lambda_{nm}}\left\{
 \sqrt{\frac{(n\vee m)\log(e(n+m))}{q}}+
 \frac{\log(e(n+m))}{q}\right\}\right].
\]
inputs: Dimensions, structural normalization, outcome scale, signal floor, and overlap.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The formula was repeated locally; the hybrid decision requires it as one coherent deterministic construction.

proposed.name: Deterministic discrete-sine fallback frame
proposed.construction:
For \(1\le i\le n\) and \(1\le k\le r\), set
\[
 (U^{\mathrm F})_{ik}=\sqrt{\frac{2}{n+1}}
 \sin\!\left(\frac{\pi ik}{n+1}\right).
\]
Thus \(U^{\mathrm F}\) is the matrix formed by the first \(r\) columns of the type-I \(n\)-dimensional discrete-sine matrix.
inputs: The row dimension and target rank.

proposed_core_edits.reason: This is the explicit law-independent estimator branch requested by the directive.

proposed.name: Observed-data IPW--sine hybrid
proposed.construction:
Using \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\) from \(\mathrm{def:loose\mbox{-}radius}\), define the observed-data hybrid
\[
 \widehat U^{\mathrm H}=
 \begin{cases}
 \widehat U^{\mathrm I},&a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\le1,\\
 U^{\mathrm F},&a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}>1.
 \end{cases}
\]
The branch predicate and \(U^{\mathrm F}\) are deterministic functions of the fixed model inputs.
inputs: The deterministic loose radius, recorded IPW--SVD fit, and sine fallback frame.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The minimax upper bound must exhibit one data map rather than select an estimator separately for each law.

proposed.name: Observed-experiment estimator class
proposed.construction:
Set \(\mathcal O_{n,m}=\sigma(A,Y,p)\) and
\[
 \mathfrak E_{n,m}=\{\widetilde U:\widetilde U\text{ is }\mathcal O_{n,m}\text{-measurable and }\widetilde U\in\mathbb O_{n,r}\}.
\]
The dimensions, the structural envelopes, and the fixed singular-vector tie rule are nonrandom inputs; measurability of an \(\mathbb O_{n,r}\)-valued map is with respect to the Borel sigma-field inherited from \(\mathbb R^{n\times r}\).
inputs: The observed assignments, outcomes, recorded propensities, and fixed nonrandom model inputs.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The clarified definition makes the estimator codomain, Borel measurability, and deterministic inputs explicit for the hybrid admissibility proof without changing the observed sigma-field.

proposed.statement:

\[

 E_P\!\left[\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm I},U)\right]
 \le C a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm},
\]
where \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\) is defined in \(\mathrm{def:loose\mbox{-}radius}\).  Thus the loose IPW--SVD upper bound holds in the same expected normalized maximum-row loss used by the minimax lower benchmark.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Close the observed-data minimax gap between the lower/reference scale \(b_{nm}\) and the constant hybrid upper endpoint, before attempting a sharp \(b_{nm}\)-normalized constant.
open_obligations.obstruction: The fixed-propensity Fano family gives only a positive multiple of \(b_{nm}\); the sine fallback gives only constant risk; and the adaptive endogenous-factor witness lower-bounds only recorded IPW--SVD, not every estimator in the observed-data class.
open_obligations.attempted: A row-local constant-propensity packing, matrix-Freedman IPW control, and the deterministic incoherent sine fallback have all been completed.  They give a valid two-sided bracket but do not reveal the information retained by an estimator that is robust to outcome-dependent future singular factors.
open_obligations.partial_result: In the lower-bound regime, \(c b_{n_\ell m_\ell}\le R^\star_\ell\le C\).  Nonemptiness forces \(\lambda_{nm}\le2B\sqrt{nm}\); at fixed \(r,\mu,K,q\) and bounded aspect ratio this yields \(b_{nm}\gtrsim\sqrt{\log n/n}\), whereas both \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\) and the blind resolution \(d_{nm}\) are at least order \(\sqrt{\log n}\).  Recorded IPW--SVD can fail at the \(b_{nm}\) scale, but this does not determine the minimax rate or \(C_\star\).

prose_updates.tldr: Recorded propensities identify the causal effect matrix and make entrywise IPW errors a bounded row-major martingale-difference array.  Write \(R_{nm}(\widetilde U)=\sup_P E_P[\mathcal L(\widetilde U,U)]\) and \(R^*_{nm}=\inf_{\widetilde U\in\mathfrak E_{n,m}}R_{nm}(\widetilde U)\).  In the stated lower-bound regime, the strongest same-assumption expected-risk result is now \(c b_{nm}\le R^*_{nm}\le R_{nm}(\widehat U^{\mathrm H})\le C(1\wedge a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm})\le C\), where \(\widehat U^{\mathrm H}\) uses recorded IPW--SVD only when its deterministic loose radius is at most one and otherwise reports an incoherent discrete-sine frame.  Bounded outcomes force \(\lambda_{nm}\le2B\sqrt{nm}\) whenever the class is nonempty.  Consequently, at fixed complexity and bounded aspect ratio, \(b_{nm}\gtrsim\sqrt{\log n/n}\) but both \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\) and the blind resolution \(d_{nm}\) are at least order \(\sqrt{\log n}\); their uniform guarantees are nonshrinking.  The adaptive witness rules out \(b_{nm}\)-attainment only for recorded IPW--SVD, so the minimax gap from \(b_{nm}\) to a constant remains open.  The rank-one \(0.25/0.75\) Markov law remains a blind-scaling stress design for HeartSteps II, and simultaneous dense-query radii retain a separate \(\sqrt{\log|\mathcal G_n|}\) multiplicity factor.

project_justification.gap: Published independent-mask rowwise matrix results do not settle causal effect-subspace risk under history-predictable assignment.  On the present effect-only low-rank class, a constant-propensity packing gives the lower/reference scale \(b_{nm}\).  The valid IPW--SVD radius is nonshrinking in every nonempty fixed-complexity bounded-aspect regime, while a deterministic incoherent fallback reduces the uniform minimax upper endpoint to a constant.  The remaining gap is therefore from \(b_{nm}\) to constant order; the accepted IPW-specific obstruction does not supply an estimator-independent converse.
project_justification.niche: The contribution is an explicit expected maximum-row minimax bracket for a causal row subspace under predictable masks, with one admissible hybrid estimator attaining the constant endpoint, together with an estimator-specific IPW obstruction, a calibrated blind-normalization resolution theorem, and conservative simultaneous causal-contrast bands whose entropy cost is separate.
project_justification.fill: The project proves a \(b_{nm}\) constant-propensity minimax lower bound, a \(C a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\) moment guarantee for recorded IPW--SVD, and a deterministic-sine hybrid guarantee \(C(1\wedge a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm})\le C\).  It derives the signal ceiling imposed by bounded outcomes and the resulting floors \(b_{nm}\gtrsim\sqrt{\log n/n}\) and \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm},d_{nm}\gtrsim\sqrt{\log n}\).  It retains the explicit Markov witness and the finite-sample direct-IPW simultaneous band with visible family-size inflation.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Recorded IPW--SVD uses the known predictable propensities and no estimated treatment nuisance.  Its matrix-Freedman guarantee is retained as \(C a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\), but bounded outcomes and the signal floor make that radius nonshrinking at fixed complexity.  The observed-data hybrid switches deterministically to an incoherent sine frame when \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}>1\), yielding constant uniform risk without changing the law class.  The blind procedure replaces entrywise propensities by a clipped empirical row fraction and remains certified only at the nonshrinking \(d_{nm}\) resolution.  Simultaneous bands use direct recorded-IPW contrasts and deterministic variance envelopes; leave-one-cell-out multiplier exactness is not claimed.

prose_updates.related_work:
Mehrotra, Tran, Vu, and Zampetakis analyze armwise empirical-row-scaled SVD under independent Bernoulli assignment and low-rank arm means.  For arm-mean matrices \(A^1\) and \(A^0\), the only algebraic implication used here is \(\operatorname{rank}(A^1-A^0)\le\operatorname{rank}(A^1)+\operatorname{rank}(A^0)\).  Its converse fails even for bounded matrices: with \(d=\min(n,m)\), take \(C=\varepsilon\sum_{k=1}^d e_k^{(n)}(e_k^{(m)})^\top\), \(D=\delta e_1^{(n)}(e_1^{(m)})^\top\), and \(0<\delta<\varepsilon\); then \(A^0=C\) and \(A^1=C+D\) are bounded and full rank \(d\), while \(A^1-A^0=D\) has rank one.  This witness establishes only failure of the converse rank implication, not containment between full statistical model classes or transfer of a rate.  Their public Theorem 3.2 and Corollary 3.3 share only the polynomial geometry \(\sqrt{n^{-1}+nm^{-2}}\): their matrix-row bound has its own fourth-power logarithmic factor and armwise assumptions, whereas \(b_{nm}\) additionally has \(\sqrt{\log n}\) and the subspace conversion \(B\sqrt{nm}/\lambda_{nm}\).

Cai, Li, Chi, Poor, and Chen give two-to-infinity upper and lower bounds for an independently sampled fixed low-rank matrix with independent noise; these inform the perturbation and packing architecture but do not resolve predictable causal subspace risk.  Hadad, Hirshberg, Zhan, Wager, and Athey support the recorded-propensity martingale-score reduction, and Tropp supplies the matrix Freedman inequality.  Dwivedi, Tian, Tomkins, Klasnja, Murphy, and Shah study adaptive nearest-neighbor arm-mean estimation under their exogenous factor conditions; their theorem has a different target and does not itself provide the present maximum-row minimax result.  Other completion and factor references concern Frobenius, entrywise, treated-cell, or fixed-missingness targets and are used only for context.

Khan and Ugander analyze scalar affine normalization under independent indicators; the blind row-fraction SVD and its \(0.25/0.75\) Markov witness are new objects here and do not refute that procedure.  Belloni and Oliveira and Ma, Niu, Zhang, and Zhu motivate high-dimensional martingale or multiplier inference, but the retained simultaneous theorem is a direct finite-sample Freedman and union-bound result.  Its \(\sqrt{\log|\mathcal G_n|}\) factor is a query-family entropy cost, not part of either subspace scale.  Spruijt-Metz et al. make saved propensities and omission sensitivity operationally relevant for the HeartSteps II consumer.

prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The frozen class allows target singular factors to depend on earlier outcomes, so rowwise leave-one-out arguments cannot treat them as predictable; the explicit obstruction shows this matters for recorded IPW--SVD.  The sine fallback removes the divergent normalized IPW upper endpoint but supplies only constant risk, leaving the estimator-independent gap \(b_{nm}\) to \(1\).  Nonemptiness plus bounded outcomes forces \(\lambda_{nm}\le2B\sqrt{nm}\); hence \(a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\) and the blind resolution \(d_{nm}\) are at least order \(\sqrt{\log n}\) for fixed \(r,\mu,K,q\) and bounded aspect ratio.  The blind tangent and ratio expansion therefore give a coarse, nonshrinking uniform diagnostic in this regime.  Separate arm means in the denominator derivative are not estimable at a claimed frontier rate under effect-only low rank, and no residual covariance consistency, positive random studentizer, or feasible multiplier exactness is assumed.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Identification is given by the recorded-IPW conditional mean.  In the stated lower-bound regime, the proved common-risk statement is \(c b_{nm}\le R^*_{nm}\le C(1\wedge a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm})\le C\), witnessed by one observed-data hybrid.  This is not a matched rate: the lower/reference scale can still vanish but, in a nonempty fixed-complexity bounded-aspect regime, cannot be smaller than order \(\sqrt{\log n/n}\), while the available uniform upper endpoint is constant.  Recorded IPW--SVD separately has the \(C a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\) moment bound and an estimator-specific \(b_{nm}\)-scale failure witness; neither implies constant-order risk for every observed-data estimator.  The blind procedure is certified only at nonshrinking \(d_{nm}\) resolution, and the \(0.25/0.75\) Markov sequence is a boundary example for that procedure and a HeartSteps II stress design.  Simultaneous inference uses conservative direct-IPW radii with separate query-family multiplicity, not feasible multiplier exactness.  Comparator discussion uses only the one-way armwise rank inequality and an explicit bounded full-rank common-component counterexample to its converse; it makes no model-containment or rate-transfer claim.

proofs.proof_tex:
Write
\[
 s_{nm}=\sqrt{n^{-1}+nm^{-2}}
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 t_{nm}=\frac{B\sqrt{nm}}{\lambda_{nm}}\sqrt{\log(en)}\,
 K r^{3/2}\mu q^{-1/2}s_{nm}.
\]
By \(\mathrm{ass:aspect\mbox{-}ratio}\),
\[
 s_{nm}
 =n^{-1/2}\sqrt{1+(n/m)^2}
 \asymp n^{-1/2}
\]
and
\[
 \sqrt{nm}\,s_{nm}
 =\sqrt{m+n^2/m}
 \asymp\sqrt n.
\]
All implicit constants in these comparisons depend only on \(c_-\) and \(c_+\).  Since \(r,\mu,K,q\) are fixed and positive, \(\mathrm{def:geometric\mbox{-}rate}\) and \(\mathrm{def:frontier\mbox{-}rate}\) give
\[
 b_{nm}=1\wedge t_{nm},
 \qquad
 t_{nm}\asymp
 \frac{B\sqrt{n\log(en)}}{\lambda_{nm}}.
\]
The hypothesis \(b_{nm}=o(1)\) implies \(b_{nm}<1\) eventually.  For such indices, \(1\wedge t_{nm}<1\) forces \(t_{nm}<1\), so \(b_{nm}=t_{nm}\).  Consequently the truncation in \(b_{nm}\) is eventually inactive and
\[
 b_{nm}\asymp
 \frac{B\sqrt{n\log(en)}}{\lambda_{nm}}.
\]

For the second radius, put
\[
 x_{nm}=\frac B{\lambda_{nm}}
 \left\{
 q^{-1}\sqrt{(n\vee m)\log(e(n+m))}
 +q^{-3}\log(en)
 \right\}.
\]
The aspect-ratio bounds imply \(n\vee m\asymp n\) and
\(\log(e(n+m))\asymp\log(en)\).  Moreover,
\[
 \frac{\log(en)}{\sqrt{n\log(en)}}
 =\sqrt{\frac{\log(en)}n}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Because \(q\) is fixed and positive, it follows that
\[
 x_{nm}\asymp
 \frac{B\sqrt{n\log(en)}}{\lambda_{nm}}
 \asymp b_{nm}=o(1).
\]
Thus \(x_{nm}<1\) eventually, so the truncation in the definition of \(d_{nm}\) is also inactive.  Hence
\[
 d_{nm}
 =\sqrt{\frac n{\mu r}}\,x_{nm}
 \asymp
 \sqrt{\frac n{\mu r}}\,b_{nm}.
\]
The quantities \(B,\lambda_{nm},q,K,r,\mu,n,m\) are positive, so \(b_{nm}>0\) and division is legitimate.  Since \(r\) and \(\mu\) are fixed,
\[
 \frac{d_{nm}}{b_{nm}}\asymp\sqrt n\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
Therefore no dimension path satisfying the stated fixed-complexity hypotheses and \(b_{nm}=o(1)\) can also satisfy \(d_{nm}=O(b_{nm})\).

added_lemmas.statement:
For every \(n,m\ge2\) such that
\[
 \mathfrak P^{\mathrm{pred}}_{n,m}(r,\mu,K,q,B,\lambda)
 \ne\varnothing.
\]
one has
\[
 \lambda_{nm}\le 2B\sqrt{nm}.
\]
Consequently, along any path on which this class is nonempty at every index, \(n\to\infty\), \(c_-\le m/n\le c_+\), and \(r,\mu,K,q\) are fixed, define
\[
 a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}
 =\sqrt{\frac n{\mu r}}
 \left[1\wedge\frac B{\lambda_{nm}}
 \left\{
 \sqrt{\frac{(n\vee m)\log(e(n+m))}{q}}
 +\frac{\log(e(n+m))}{q}
 \right\}\right]
\]
and
\[
 d_{nm}
 =\sqrt{\frac n{\mu r}}
 \left[1\wedge\frac B{\lambda_{nm}}
 \left\{
 q^{-1}\sqrt{(n\vee m)\log(e(n+m))}
 +q^{-3}\log(en)
 \right\}\right].
\]
For all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 b_{nm}\ge
 \frac{K r^{3/2}\mu}{2\sqrt q}
 \sqrt{\frac{\log(en)}n},
\]
\[
 a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}\ge
 \frac{1}{2\sqrt{c_+q\mu r}}\sqrt{\log(en)},
 \qquad
 d_{nm}\ge
 \frac{1}{2q\sqrt{c_+\mu r}}\sqrt{\log(en)}.
\]
In particular, the last two uniform radii are nonshrinking and in fact diverge at least at order \(\sqrt{\log n}\).
